overview: Hepatitis B is a viral infection that attacks the liver and can cause both acute and chronic disease. It can spread through contact with infected body fluids like blood, saliva, vaginal fluids and semen. Hepatitis B can be prevented with a safe and effective vaccine.
symptoms: yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice)
transmission: contact with infected blood or body fluids
sharing or reuse of contaminated needles and syringes
prevention: linkage to prevention and care and treatment services
risk_factors: infection in infancy and early childhood
partners or family members of infected persons
people in prisons and other closed settings
men who have sex with men
key_facts: 254 million people were living with chronic hepatitis B infection in 2022
1.1 million deaths in 2022, mostly from cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma
97 million people are chronically infected in the WHO Western Pacific Region
65 million people are chronically infected in the WHO African Region
